html:
e-Estonia is the name for Estonia's push since the late 1990s to run almost all public services online. It made it one of the most digital states in the world.

Starting almost from scratch after independence, the government put computers in all schools and in 2001 built X-Road, a secure network that links state and private databases. Every resident has a digital ID card used to sign documents, file taxes in minutes and see medical records. In 2005 it became the first country to let all voters vote over the internet, in local elections, and in 2007 in a national one. In 2014 it began e-residency for foreigners.

Tech firms such as Skype grew from the same culture. The cyberattacks of 2007 showed the risks, and NATO set up its cyber defence centre in Tallinn. See Estonia.
sum: e-Estonia is the name for Estonia's push since the late 1990s to run almost all public services online. It made it one of the most digital states in the world.
